events.what: pilgrimage (Benares, Rameswaram, Guruvayur) and charity as shanti, begun when the Jupiter bhukti started
birth of a child, born in Moolam star (Kethu star in Jupiter's sign Sagittarius)
events.dasa: Kethu dasa, Jupiter bhukti (before it ended)

notes: Partial chart in prose only. Lagna not printed. The lagna lord is Jupiter, so the lagna is Sagittarius or Pisces. Inference (not printed): with sign-based houses only Sagittarius works, because then the 5th is Aries and the 6th lord is Venus, so Rahu and Saturn would be in Bharani. With a Pisces lagna the 5th would be Cancer and the 6th lord the Sun, which has no star in Cancer. Kethu, opposite Rahu, would then be in Libra (Swathi/Visakha). Used for Krishnamurti's rule that the Moon's star and sub at a child's birth are those of the parent's dasa and bhukti lords or their star lords (KP2-220), and for the karma/shanti discussion (KP2-230…232).

planets.Rahu: Tau 26°36' (printed "Taurus at 26° - 36°"): Venus sign, Mars star Mrigasira, Jupiter sub

events.what: appointed manager in an automobile industry
events.dasa: Rahu dasa, Jupiter bhukti, Venus anthra, Mars sookshma

notes: Only Rahu's position is printed. Arithmetic check: Taurus 26°36' = 56°36' absolute. Mrigasira starts at 53°20'; its subs run Mars to 54°06'40", Rahu to 56°06'40", Jupiter to 57°53'20". So the Jupiter sub is correct. The dasa chain is Rahu (planet), its sub lord, its sign lord and its star lord: Rahu as agent of sign, star and sub lords (KP2-052).

events.what: exports human hair collected at famous temples

notes: Printed: 'born [in] Cancer having Sun in Karthik 1st pada aspected by exalted Saturn'. It does not say whether 'Cancer' is the lagna or the Moon sign. If Cancer is the lagna, Aries is the 10th, so the Sun is in the 10th, opposite Saturn in the 4th. Illustrates Sun + Saturn = wool and hair (KP2-200).

events.what: George III ascended the throne; Samuel Hennings set up as an independent businessman
both married on the same day (Hennings married Elsie)

notes: The classic 'astro-twins' story (George III and Samuel Hennings), quoted from a foreign journal of 1820. Hennings is said to have died aged 82. B2 gives Hennings's birth date as 4-6-1738, which is also George III's birth date (4 June 1738, London). No time or chart printed. Used for 'identical results for identical birth moment and place' (KP2-213).
